I don't think so. I think it's something a bit more simple. There's an apt quote from Bertrand Russell, "The fundamental cause of the trouble in the modern world today is that the stupid are cocksure while the intelligent are full of doubt." Take something like climate change. If you ask 100 people their opinion here, the degree of nuance and uncertainty is going to be directly proportional to their understanding of the topic.

Put another way, the people that have no idea about the topic are going to be 100% positively certain one way or the other. "Nope, humans have no clear role in this. Climate always changes." to "Yes, we are definitely responsible for it. If we don't go green in the next 10 years the world will absolutely and positively face catastrophic consequences within the next 50." They're two sides of the same coin of ignorance.

But most people are not well informed on most topics. And so they're drawn to more simplistic views. And in social media where what reaches the top is not judged on merit, but popularity, you end up seeing all the worst of society float to the top. So I think what you see as trending or popular says relatively little about the intelligence of society as a whole. We've just gone from a world where only the relatively elite were able to have a voice to one where any and everyone can share their views with the rest of the world.
